thread:
maya: Quick sanity scan for sparrowhawk-v1 embeddings. ran a small wiki50k holdout (5k queries) to compare fp16 baseline -> 6-bit per-channel -> 4-bit per-layer. posting highlevel numbers and a couple pointers.

jon: pls paste the numbers, quick glance only needed.

maya: ```
model                recall@1  recall@5  recall@10  silhouette
sparrowhawk-fp16     0.712     0.853     0.892      0.412
sparrowhawk-6bit     0.708     0.848     0.889      0.403
sparrowhawk-4bit     0.692     0.827     0.869      0.356
```

maya: Notes: 6-bit per-channel is within noise (~0.4% drop @1) and silhouette ~0.009 lower. 4-bit shows a clear degradation esp for short queries (<10 tokens) where recall@1 drops ~3% absolute.

jon: interesting — did you use per-channel quant or per-tensor?

maya: per-channel for 6-bit, 4-bit was mixed per-layer fallback to keep perf. used PQ-free path for eval (no PQ).

liam: which index settings? IVF/HNSW?
maya: IVF4096 + HNSW overlay (M=32, efConstruction=200). nprobe=32 in the baseline run.

eva: did you check cluster visuals? UMAP / silhouette plots?
maya: UMAP shows several topic clusters merging for 4-bit. silhouette drop matches that. attaching quick screenshot link (private): <https://internal/redwood-artifacts/sparrowhawk/umap-4bit.png>

jon: any idea if this is quantization bias or collapsed norms?
maya: looks like norm collapse on a subset. when normalizing before index, 4-bit improves a bit (recall@1 +0.8%), but still worse than fp16. 6-bit behaves almost identical to fp16 with L2 norm.

liam: can you run a follow-up with nprobe=64 and scalar-quant-rescale on 4-bit? i want to see if retrieval params hide the drop.
maya: queued. command i used: ```bash
python tools/eval_embeddings.py \
  --model sparrowhawk-v1 \
  --quant 4bit \
  --dataset wiki50k \
  --index ivf4096_hnsw \
  --nprobe 32 \
  --batch 2048 \
  --metrics recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,silhouette
```

liam: thx. also run the same with batching disabled (batch=1) for the encoder to see if micro-batching/FP accumulation masks precision issues.

maya: will run both. ETA ~45m.

jon: we should also run holdout stratified by query length and by entity density (short vs multi-entity docs). sounds like short queries are the pain point.

maya: agreed — stratified splits planned. quick strat results from initial run: recall@1 for queries<10 tokens: fp16=0.694, 6bit=0.689, 4bit=0.661. for queries>40 tokens: fp16=0.741, 6bit=0.738, 4bit=0.731.

eva: do we have any downstream ranking/regression tests? small rerank eval would show impact on final UX.
maya: not yet for this model. next step after triage.

liam: if 6-bit is that close, could be our default quant profile for Dedicated until we resolve 4-bit path. lower mem with acceptable delta.
